scoringCalibration: One point is awarded to face identity and forms. The face now has stronger orbital support, zygomatic projection, tear-trough recession, buccal transition, nasolabial structure, mental sulcus and chin separation without changing topology or creating attachment intersections.
visualFindings: The zygomatic region reads as a distinct plane instead of one broad smooth cheek.
The tear trough, infraorbital support and buccal recession create a more legible eye-to-cheek transition.
The mental sulcus and chin pad separate the lower lip region from the chin.
The changes remain restrained at a maximum local displacement of 1.04 mm and preserve the established silhouette.
rejectedExperiments: Keeping the old brow-density, upper-fold and tear-line positions was rejected after the first v52 audit found body intersections.
Discarding the facial-plane sculpt was rejected because reprojecting the six affected surface layers removed every neutral and posed intersection without weakening the new anatomy.
blockingFailures: The face still needs expression-oriented perioral loops, asymmetric commissure sculpting and a phoneme pose suite.
Integrated upper and lower eyelid thickness and expression-compatible canthus topology remain below review quality.
The crown needs a coherent authored direction field with a narrower irregular part and fewer cross-flow fibers.
Hair shading still needs an engine-side dual-lobe anisotropic model and strand-scale roughness variation.
Clothing edge flow, seams, folds, materials and outer layers remain below review quality.
Raised-arm shoulders still require corrective deformation and the standard pose suite remains incomplete.
Signed clothing-distance samples remain negative despite zero exact triangle overlaps in the audited frames.
LOD transition popping and frame-time impact remain untested in the website renderer.
